subject: English
topic: Active and Passive Voice — Change of Voice

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: 'She writes a letter.'

options.option_text: A letter was written by her.
A letter is written by her.
A letter is being written by her.
A letter has been written by her.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Active Simple Present: Subject + V(s/es) + Object → Passive: Object + is/am/are + V3 (past participle) + by + Subject. 'She writes a letter' → 'A letter IS WRITTEN by her.' Tense marker: is/are (present) + V3.

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: 'They were building a new bridge.'

options.option_text: A new bridge was built by them.
A new bridge was being built by them.
A new bridge is being built by them.
A new bridge had been built by them.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Active Past Continuous: was/were + V-ing → Passive: was/were + being + V3. 'They were building' → 'was being built.' Summary of auxiliary in passive: Simple Present → is/are V3; Past → was/were V3; Present Continuous → is/are being V3; Past Continuous → was/were being V3.

questions.stem: Change to Active Voice: 'The letter has been signed by the manager.'

options.option_text: The manager signed the letter.
The manager has signed the letter.
The manager signs the letter.
The manager was signing the letter.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Passive Present Perfect = has/have been + V3. Converting to Active: Agent (the manager) becomes subject + has/have + V3. 'Has been signed by the manager' → 'The manager HAS SIGNED the letter.' Reverse conversion must preserve the tense indicated by the auxiliary.

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: 'Who wrote this novel?'

options.option_text: By whom was this novel written?
By who was this novel written?
This novel was written by who?
Was this novel written by whom?

questions.explanation: A is correct. For questions with 'WHO' as subject in active: Active: 'Who wrote this novel?' → Passive: 'By WHOM was this novel written?' Change: 'Who' → 'By whom'; object→subject; apply passive tense. 'Whom' is the correct objective case form (used after prepositions like 'by').

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: 'The company will launch a new product next month.'

options.option_text: A new product is launched by the company next month.
A new product will be launched by the company next month.
A new product would be launched by the company next month.
A new product is going to be launched by the company next month.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Future Simple Passive = will be + V3. 'Will launch' → 'will be launched.' Passive voice auxiliary map: will + V1 → will be + V3; would + V1 → would be + V3; can + V1 → can be + V3; must + V1 → must be + V3.

options.option_text: She has been working here for five years.
The windows have been cleaned.
He will have left by then.
They were watching a movie.

questions.explanation: B is correct. A PASSIVE VOICE sentence has the structure: object + auxiliary (be-verb) + V3 (past participle). 'The windows have been CLEANED' = subject + have been + V3 → passive. The agent (who cleaned) is not mentioned. All others are active where the subject performs the action.

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: 'Please open the door.'

options.option_text: The door should be opened.
Let the door be opened.
The door is opened.
The door was opened.

questions.explanation: B is correct. IMPERATIVE → Passive: 'Let + object + be + V3.' 'Open the door' → 'Let THE DOOR BE OPENED.' 'Please' is dropped in passive. 'Let them do it' → 'Let it be done by them.' This is a frequently tested conversion in SSC exams.

questions.stem: Which sentence correctly converts 'I know her.' to passive voice?

options.option_text: She is knowing by me.
She is known to me.
She is known by me.
She has been known by me.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Some stative verbs use 'TO' instead of 'BY' in passive: know→'known TO me'; surprise→'surprised AT'; please→'pleased WITH'; interest→'interested IN'; contain→'contained IN'. 'I know her' → 'She IS KNOWN TO ME' (not 'by me'). This is a tricky exception tested in exams.

questions.stem: Change to Active Voice: 'English is spoken all over the world.'

options.option_text: People speak English all over the world.
English speaks all over the world.
All over the world, English is being spoken.
English was spoken all over the world.

questions.explanation: A is correct. When no agent is mentioned in passive (no 'by...'), use 'People/They/One' as the general subject in active voice. 'English is spoken' (passive, no agent) → 'PEOPLE SPEAK English all over the world' (active). This is the standard approach for agentless passive sentences.

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: 'She can solve this problem.'

options.option_text: This problem is solvable by her.
This problem can be solved by her.
This problem could be solved by her.
This problem can have been solved by her.

questions.explanation: B is correct. MODAL PASSIVE: Modal (can/could/will/would/should/must/may/might) + be + V3. 'Can solve' → 'CAN BE SOLVED.' Complete map: can→can be; could→could be; will→will be; should→should be; must→must be; may→may be; might→might be.
